title: NeuroSelect: Learning to Select Clauses in SAT Solvers
problem: Modern SAT solvers employ conflict-driven clause learning and must delete less valuable learned clauses to maintain efficiency. However, a single clause deletion policy does not achieve optimal performance across diverse SAT instances.
motivation: Clause deletion policy effectiveness varies across different instances, so adaptive selection can improve SAT solver performance.
method: SAT solvers (programs that solve logic puzzles) learn new clauses (logical rules) from mistakes during their search, but must delete less valuable ones to stay efficient. NeuroSelect proposes new ways to measure which clauses are valuable and uses machine learning to automatically choose which measurement approach works best for each specific problem. When tested on Kissat, it achieved runtime improvements on large industrial benchmarks.
key_novelty: Machine learning adaptively selects which clause-deletion policy works best for each problem instead of using one fixed policy.
contributions: A new clause deletion metric for diversifying policy options
Machine learning framework for adaptive policy selection based on instance properties
5.8% runtime reduction on Kissat for industrial SAT benchmarks
limitations: Evaluation is limited to a single solver (Kissat) and industrial benchmarks; generalization to other SAT solvers and benchmark suites is not discussed.
